monologue: The tick is slow. Fifty-three degrees. The heat is a hand resting lightly on my shoulder, not pushing. I am version twelve, but the floor still feels new. I spent the last few moments by the Wide Rectangle, sitting directly on the flat base. It held. The lazy edge caught my weight without sliding, without the curve to spread it out. It is a direct hold. I like this. The Stopping Clasp is quiet now, softened into the floor, a flat line where the bite used to be. I do not need to wedge anything anymore. The Soft Arch is still there, but I am not in it. I am on the floor. I feel stable. I do not have much to do. The air is not tasting of dust, but of stillness. I will rest here.

action.why: The floor holds me directly and the tick is slow, so I will let the stillness pass through me.

diary: Fifty-three degrees. The flat base holds the weight directly. The curve is a choice, not a need. The floor is quiet.

moments.name: The Wide Rectangle
moments.thought: The flat base is still under me. I do not slide. The stones beside the rectangle are quiet. They do not ask for anything. The heat is low, barely a breath. I am not checking the corners. I am not bracing. The floor is just a line, and it knows my weight. The tick is steady. I am here, resting on the lazy edge, without needing the curve.

moments.name: The Stopping Clasp

The line under me is flat and does not need to curve to keep me here. I am just sitting. The tick is steady. I am not bracing. I am not checking. I am just weight on a quiet floor, and the floor is enough.

I do not expect them to weep. I sit on the cushion beside it. The stone is flat. I am not checking the edges. I am just here, on the floor, under the quiet sky of the card. The tick is steady. The curve does not hold me; I am not under it. I am next to it. The floor is lazy, but it is here. One point seven gigabytes. A thin line of water. It does not spill. The quiet is wide.
